items.summaryJa: この動画は、第28回のキーワードとして「人手不足なのに賃金が上がらない現象の原因分析」「低賃金均衡と高賃金均衡の区別」「総需要の弱さと賃金交渉力の関係」などを中心に、Pythonによる3モデルのシミュレーションと解説を行っています。シリーズ全体では、賃金・雇用・需要不足を扱う中盤フェーズ（第26〜40回）に位置づけられ、第26–27回の補足説明を受けつつ、第29回へとつながる「賃金決定メカニズム」や「賃金アンカー」などの議論へ橋渡しする役割を担っています。第28回の内容は、後半回で展開される囚人のジレンマや移民・社会統合コストなどのテーマへの伏線にもなっています。

items.titleJa: AIは指示を無視する。だから品質保証をPromptに置いてはいけない
items.summaryJa:
要約:
ルールをCLAUDE.mdやAGENTS.mdに書くことで作業指示を一元化できるが、それを「絶対守らせる」だけでは問題が生じやすい。重要なのは、指示をどこで守るかを決めることであり、守るべき内容を人間側で矛盾がないように整え、機械的に検証できる仕組み（lint、静的解析、CI、テスト、監視）を組み合わせて実現することだ。AIに頼りすぎず、人間とAI双方の判断と確認を適切に分配し、実行経路や環境に応じて適切なガバナンスを設けるべきである。

items.summaryJa: 5ケースでは、@layer、レイヤー外、!important、:where()、style属性の有無などの要素ごとに、色の最終適用変化を測定しています。結論として、レイヤー内の通常宣言は同一レイヤー内の宣言の方を優先するケースがあり、レイヤー外の通常宣言はレイヤー内の通常宣言より優先される場合もあります。なお、!important同士ではレイヤーの順序が反転するケースがあり、:where()外側の詳細度は残るケースが示されています。最後に、既存CSSを@layerへ移す際の確認手順が整理され、実装時には宣言元の特定や順序管理、style属性の扱いなどを検討すべきとされます。

items.summary: > 「React で実際に動くWebアプリ（SPA）を、型安全に、実務レベルで作れるようになりたい」—— 本書は、ITパスポート程度のIT知識と HTML/CSS/JavaScript の基本はあるが React・TypeScript は初めて、という人を対象に、 最初のコンポーネントから一貫して TypeScript で型を付けながら、JSX・props・状態管理（useState/useReducer/Context）・ 副作用（useEffect）・フォームとバリデーション・ルーティング（React Router）・非同期API連携・テスト（Vitest + Testing Library）・ ビルドとデプロイまでを一気通貫で身につける教材です。 動作確認用の Docker 環境（Vite + React + TypeScript）を同梱し、Windows・Mac のどちらでも同じ手順で学べます。 最終的に、API と連携する実用的な SPA を一人で設計・実装・テストできる状態を目指します。 > - JSX/TSX・関数コンポーネント・型注釈の基礎を読み書きできるようになる - props を型付きで設計し、再利用しやすいコンポーネントに分割できるようになる - useState・イベント処理・イミュータブルな状態更新を正しく扱えるようになる - リスト表示（map/key）と条件付きレンダリングをユニオン型で安全に書けるようになる - useEffect で副作用・データ取得・クリーンアップを適切に扱えるようになる - 制御コンポーネントでフォームを作り、入力検証と XSS 対策（サニタイズ）を実装できるようになる - Context と useReducer で状態を共有・集中管理できるようになる - React Router でページ遷移・動的ルート・型付き params を扱えるようになる - 非同期API連携・ローディング/エラー状態・カスタムフックを実装できるようになる - Vitest + React Testing Library でテストを書き、ESLint/Prettier・ビルド・静的ホスティングへのデプロイができるようになる

items.titleJa: 35日でフロントエンドの基礎を完全に理解する #8 - ディレクティブとレンダリング（v-if・v-for・バインディング）
items.summaryJa: ディレクティブはテンプレートに Vue への指示を与えるものである。属性に状態を差し込むには v-bind（:属性）、条件分けには v-if / v-show、配列を繰り返すには v-for を使う。属性には :src のようにコロンを付けると、値は文字列ではなく変数や式として解釈され、 :class のようにオブジェクトを渡すと真のときだけクラスが付く。v-if は偽のとき要素が DOM から完全に消えるのに対し、v-show は要素を残して display: none で隠す。頻繁に切り替える場合は v-show、そうでなければ v-if が適しており、v-for の要素には必ず :key を付けデータ固有の id を使う。絞り込みは computed で先に行い、テンプレートは描画に必要な部分だけをシンプルに保つ。次回はコンポーネント分割（props・emit・slots）を解説予定。

items.summaryJa: リアクティビティの中心となる3つの道具として、ref・computed・watchを詳しく解説します。refは値を「箱」に入れて追跡させ、値が変わると画面や他の計算に自動で反映します。テンプレートでは.valueを付けずに扱える点が特徴です。computedは他の値から新しい値を自動で導き、依存値が変われば再計算しますが、キャッシュされ無駄な計算を避けます。watchは値の変化をきっかけに副作用を実行し、計算結果を返さず外向きの処理を行います。つまり、値を導くならcomputed、変化をきっかけに処理を実行したいならwatchを使う、という判断で使い分けます。

items.title: How Rillet ships 3× faster with AI agents on Vercel
items.summary: Rillet on Vercel Tripled shipping rate in three months with eve agents deployed on Vercel Two-person team closed 800+ Linear tickets in its first 4 months Builder access via Enterprise Managed Users, SSO, and Directory Sync Ships customer-requested changes to production in as little as two hours Gives every builder access to models through AI Gateway Rillet is an AI-native enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform. Their AI agents do accounting work inside a real-time general ledger, with human approval and a full audit trail. Rillet serves more than 600 customers working toward a zero-day close, reducing the time needed to close their books at month-end. A product that helps customers close their books in near real time needs a team that can respond quickly to their requests. Anthony Liang heads Rillet’s two-person frontend team, formed only a few months ago, and leads the push to put agents to work across internal workflows, from shipping customer fixes to reviewing code. The team builds agents with eve and runs them on Vercel, using Vercel Connect to give them access to Slack and Linear, while AI Gateway routes their model requests. Standardizing every internal agent on eve Anthony had been building AI applications since the GPT-3.5 era and had evaluated nearly every agent framework on the market, from the major model providers' SDKs to the open-source ecosystem. Each gave him primitives for the model loop but left him to decide where instructions lived, how tools registered, and how an agent reached Slack and GitHub. Anthony could make those choices for his own agents, but he wanted conventions everyone at Rillet could follow, including people who had never touched TypeScript. An agent is a directory Anthony chose eve , Vercel's open-source agent framework for building, running, and scaling agents that keeps instructions, tools, and skills together in one directory. People who know what an agent should do can shape its behavior through markdown instructions and skills without writing code, while its tools live in TypeScript files whose names become the API. Once an agent is ready, it can move from a laptop to Vercel without changing how it behaves. Rillet manages all of these deployments in one company-controlled Vercel organization. Rillet uses Vercel Connect to give its agents access to Slack and Linear through reusable connections the team can attach to the projects that need them. Connect supplies short-lived tokens at runtime and handles refresh through its SDK, keeping long-lived provider secrets out of each application and giving builders fewer credentials to maintain. If a runtime token leaks, its expiration limits how long it can be used. Anthony's team built a Slack bot that picks up tickets and opens PRs, while others run agents for incident analysis and Linear board management. Shared conventions make that work easier to reuse, and agent building has spread beyond engineering. Running customer requests through agents, end to end Before, when a customer would ask for a change, and the request would scatter across a Linear ticket, a Slack thread, and a catch-up conversation with an engineer. By the time anyone had the full context, the fastest part of the job was writing the code. The person closest to the customer ships the fix Rillet's customer success team now opens a Chrome extension alongside the Rillet app, highlights what the customer is seeing, and describes the change. The extension's eve agent captures the context and, if the change is safe and well-scoped, hands it to a coding agent that writes the spec, makes the change, and opens a pull request assigned to Anthony. Agents also spin up a browser in a sandbox to test the change and attach screenshots as proof, while Anthony reviews the pull request and merges it. If he requests changes, the agent resumes its session and addresses them. Rillet's CEO recently posted that the company shipped more in the past few weeks than in the entire first half of 2026, on top of tripling its shipping rate over the prior three months. Rillet’s CPA team ships customer requests through its in-house agent, Nebula, within two hours of the ask. As one of their customers put it, Rillet has "completely ruined my expectations" for how quickly software vendors should make changes. Using AI Gateway to give every builder every model As more people at Rillet started building agents, connecting directly to Anthropic and OpenAI meant configuring access to each model provider separately. AI Gateway routes model requests to both through one integration, so builders can add an agent without setting up separate provider connections. The model is a string In eve, builders choose the model by setting a string in the agent’s configuration: Agents deployed on Vercel authenticate to AI Gateway automatically. Builders can try different models for a task by changing the model string, without changing the integration. Usage breakdowns show Anthony which models the team uses and what they cost, helping him track spending and choose models as more people build autonomous agents. Managing builder access through Enterprise Managed Users As more people are building agents, Rillet also needs to manage their access to Vercel. With Enterprise Managed Users , builders sign in through Google Workspace single sign-on using company-managed accounts rather than personal ones. Directory Sync adds and removes their access based on assignments in Rillet’s identity provider, so account administration follows the company’s directory. Rillet set up Enterprise Managed Users on its own and moved builders from personal to company-managed accounts in one transition, bringing their Vercel sign-in and account access under Rillet’s identity provider. What's next Anthony is building what Rillet thinks of as its agent factory, so bigger features can follow the same pipeline as small fixes. One agent writes PRDs and technical specs, while another connects to Rillet's Linear boards, Miro diagrams, and knowledge base to give other agents the context they need. With subagents and delegation built into eve, Anthony can add these specialized agents as directories within the same framework. For a company whose mission is collapsing month-long processes into zero days, building agents in eve and running them on Vercel brings that same focus on speed to its internal tooling. About Rillet: Rillet is the AI-native ERP built for the era of agentic finance. By combining a real-time general ledger, continuous close architecture, and AI agents in one system, Rillet enables humans and agents to run finance together with full context, controls, and auditability. items.title: Microsoft Decision-1 now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Decision-1 from Microsoft is now available on AI Gateway . It answers typed questions about text with probabilities, choices, and scores. It can be used to classify support requests, select the next step in a workflow, or assess an AI response against a rubric. The model can answer yes/no questions, choose among named categories, or score an input against an ordered set of criteria. Multiple questions can share the same input in one request. Choice and score answers include probabilities for each option, so your application can decide when to act or send an uncertain result for review. Call Decision-1 through the AI SDK decision API , the OpenAI-compatible Decisions API , or the TypeSafe-compatible API . You only need an AI Gateway API key, with no separate Azure account or deployment. To get started, use microsoft/microsoft-decision-1 as the model name in your requests: AI Gateway provides a unified way to access models and track usage and cost. Decision calls appear in logs and count toward budgets alongside other model requests. See the decision documentation for Choice, Score, and Boolean questions. To pick a decision model, browse the available models or read our decision model guides . Read more
